lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: folding, hanging, and matching

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 2: Clothing and Laundry Care
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice folding, hanging, and matching. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A full load of clean, dry laundry from your household is ready to be put away.
safetyNotes: If put-away requires a step stool or reaching a high closet rod, an adult in the household should handle the reaching or supervise directly rather than let the learner climb to reach it.
Handle hangers carefully, keeping the hook end pointed away from the face and eyes while hanging items.
If an item's storage spot is unclear or shared with someone else's belongings, check with a trusted adult before deciding where it goes.

simulationAlternative.description: If a full load of laundry or the actual storage space is not available, the learner instead sorts a small set of picture cards or a written list of garment types (t-shirt, dress shirt, towel, pair of socks) into fold-or-hang decisions, matches any listed pairs, and writes where each item's real storage spot would be, checked by a trusted adult in their household.

materials: learner-local: a full load of clean, dry laundry
adult-or-local: the household's real storage spaces (drawers, closet, shelves)

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain one way today's task is more specific than 'put items back where they belong' from the five-minute tidy: what extra decision did folding, hanging, and matching add that a quick tidy skips?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Fold, hang, and match technique: Each item type uses one consistent fold or hang method, and all pairs are correctly matched. | Fold-versus-hang reasoning: The explanation correctly ties the fold-or-hang decision to a specific property, such as fabric weight, shape retention, or garment type, of each item. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner build a short written fold-or-hang rule of thumb covering at least four garment types, then test the rule against one new item type not covered in today's load to see whether the rule still holds up.

resources.title: folding, hanging, and matching worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A full load of clean, dry laundry from your household is ready to be put away.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact folding, hanging, and matching decision or action.
Model move 2: Before folding or hanging anything, sort the clean load into two piles: items that get folded and items that get hung.
Model move 3: Fold each item in the fold pile using a consistent method for its type, hang each item in the hang pile, and match any paired items like socks before putting anything away.

Model check: Fold, hang, and match technique: Each item type uses one consistent fold or hang method, and all pairs are correctly matched. | Fold-versus-hang reasoning: The explanation correctly ties the fold-or-hang decision to a specific property, such as fabric weight, shape retention, or garment type, of each item.

resources.title: folding, hanging, and matching action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for folding, hanging, and matching.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: folding, hanging, and matching coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A full load of clean, dry laundry from your household is ready to be put away.
Coach direction: Before folding or hanging anything, sort the clean load into two piles: items that get folded and items that get hung.
Learner prompt: Name one item you are unsure about and explain what is making the fold-or-hang decision hard for that specific piece.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: folding, hanging, and matching complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Fold each item in the fold pile using a consistent method for its type, hang each item in the hang pile, and match any paired items like socks before putting anything away.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I folded every item in the fold pile using one consistent method per item type.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I hung every item in the hang pile so it would not slip off or stretch out of shape.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I matched every pair, like socks, before putting them away, with no unmatched singles left out unless truly missing a pair.

Equal-access rule: If a full load of laundry or the actual storage space is not available, the learner instead sorts a small set of picture cards or a written list of garment types (t-shirt, dress shirt, towel, pair of socks) into fold-or-hang decisions, matches any listed pairs, and writes where each item's real storage spot would be, checked by a trusted adult in their household.

resources.title: folding, hanging, and matching minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain one way today's task is more specific than 'put items back where they belong' from the five-minute tidy: what extra decision did folding, hanging, and matching add that a quick tidy skips?

Success checks: Fold, hang, and match technique: Each item type uses one consistent fold or hang method, and all pairs are correctly matched. | Fold-versus-hang reasoning: The explanation correctly ties the fold-or-hang decision to a specific property, such as fabric weight, shape retention, or garment type, of each item.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: folding, hanging, and matching supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional folding, hanging, and matching condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Fold, hang, and match technique: Each item type uses one consistent fold or hang method, and all pairs are correctly matched. | Fold-versus-hang reasoning: The explanation correctly ties the fold-or-hang decision to a specific property, such as fabric weight, shape retention, or garment type, of each item..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
